title: In a boost to Finland’s Loviisa plant, Google and Fortum ink nuclear PPA
summary: Google and Nordic energy company Fortum have reached a multidecade nuclear power purchase agreement (PPA) that will provide the tech giant power from Finland’s Loviisa plant through 2050, the two companies announced Wednesday. The PPA further justifies Finland’s 2023 decision to extend Loviisa’s operating license until the end of 2050. Since the 2023 decision, Fortum has adopted a life extension investment program to support the plant for another couple of decades. According to Fortum, the investments are expected to reach €1 billion (approximately $1.16 billion) by 2050. Work is already underway, including a major turbine modernization project that will be implemented during outages in 2026 and 2028.

title: NASA solicits lunar radioisotope power
summary: NASA has announced it is seeking proposals for five technological areas, including radioisotope power systems (RPSs), to support exploration missions with a near-term focus on a base at the south lunar pole.

title: West Virginia joins the ranks of NLIC finalists
summary: Earlier this week, West Virginia Gov. Patrick Morrissey announced that his state has been selected as a finalist for the Department of Energy’s Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses (NLIC) program. It joins five other finalists—Idaho, Louisiana, Oklahoma, Tennessee, and Utah—all of which are now in the running to host a facility or facilities supporting the back end of the fuel cycle through federal-state partnerships.

title: Entergy protects endangered whooping cranes while increasing reliability for customers
summary: Entergy is partnering with the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries and Fulcrum Air to deploy bird flight diverters on transmission lines across Louisiana, marking a significant milestone in the company’s commitment to protecting the endangered whooping cranes while improving reliability for our customers. title: Entergy, Ampirical invest $1.5M in LSU New Orleans Energy Lab
summary: LSU New Orleans students preparing for careers in engineering and the energy industry will gain access to enhanced technology, research opportunities and hands-on learning through a combined $1.5 million investment from Entergy and Ampirical to modernize the university’s Power and Energy Research Laboratory.
